headline: Markets hold near highs but brace for Warsh's Jackson Hole test
body: Equities enter Friday near record territory but showing cracks beneath the surface. Thursday's close saw the Nasdaq Composite jump 1.57% to 26,541, the S&P 500 add 0.72% to 7,731, and the Dow gain 0.2% to 53,569, powered by another strong Nvidia earnings beat that reinforced the AI-capex narrative. That enthusiasm hasn't carried fully into Friday's premarket, though: S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures are both slightly negative as Marvell Technology's post-earnings slide of more than 7% offsets the Nvidia lift, while Dow and Russell 2000 futures inch higher. The split reads less like broad risk-off than a market digesting mixed chip-sector results one name at a time.

The bigger overhang is macro: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote today, with investors watching for any hint the Fed is still prepared to raise rates if inflation doesn't cool, after Boston Fed President Susan Collins flagged similar risk this week. Warsh has a track record of minimal forward guidance, so the uncertainty itself is keeping Treasuries on edge following last week's long-yield highs. Options positioning still leans complacent by the most recent CBOE put/call readings, a setup that historically warrants some caution near highs. Retail chatter, meanwhile, stays concentrated rather than broad -- Reddit and social trackers show attention clustered on Nvidia and Amazon alongside a sudden spike in Intel and Micron mentions, suggesting sentiment is trading the AI/chip theme more than expressing a market-wide view.
